caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000568
attempts.paper_title: Probing subthreshold dynamics of hippocampal neurons by pulsed optogenetics
attempts.entry_title: Pulsed optogenetics in hippocampal CA1 (Valero et al. 2022)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Valero, Zutshi, Yoon and Buzsaki (2022) on dandiset 000568, which holds 28 sessions of CA1 units recorded with uLED probes in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice. Pulse times and laps are in two sessions only, so the light responses during ripples, theta and place fields are tested on those two; the ripple modulation of firing is tested on all sessions. The intracellular recordings and the light intensity levels are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Valero et al. (2022) from dandiset 000568

outcomes.statement: CA1 pyramidal neurons were recorded and probed in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice, 822 pyramidal neurons in all, 43.3 plus or minus 8.37 per session.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: we recorded and probed large numbers of CA1 pyramidal neurons simultaneously in freely moving ... n = 822 pyramidal neurons in four mice; 43.3 ± 8.37 pyramidal neurons per session
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), all 28 sessions, 4 mice and 48.2 putative pyramidal cells per session (SD 12.18) match, but the total is 1351 against 822. Under reading (b), the 22 sessions naming the uLED protocol, 3 mice, 1047 cells and 47.6 per session. 822 cells at 43.3 per session would be about 19 sessions. With thresholds of 2.5 and 10 Hz the total is 1205 or 1441.
deviations: Pyramidal cells are units with a baseline rate below 5 Hz, as the files carry no cell type; the paper classified cells by other features.
The paper does not say which sessions it used; two readings are shown.

outcomes.statement: uLEDs were driven with 20 ms pulses at random sites with randomly variable 20 to 40 ms offsets, so that the stimulation of each site recurred at about 0.3 to 0.6 s intervals.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 2; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: μLEDs were activated (0.02 to 0.1 μW, 20 ms duration) with randomly variable (20 to 40 ms) offsets so that stimulation of each site reccurred at ~0.3- to 0.6-s intervals
outcomes.notes: Pulses last 19.87 ms (sess9) and 19.63 ms (sess12). The median interval between pulses of one uLED is 0.281 to 0.383 s for the four uLEDs with at least 1000 pulses, within 0.27 to 0.66 s. The median offset from the end of one pulse to the start of the next is 60.4 and 80.0 ms, outside 18 to 44 ms; 31.8% and 30.2% of offsets fall within 20 to 40 ms, and the 95th percentiles are 241 and 328 ms. Most pulses are not in the files (5.76 and 7.50 deposited pulses per s in PreStim against about 17 to 25 implied by the protocol; in sess9 the offsets fall only near multiples of 20 ms), so the longer offsets span missing pulses and the protocol's offsets cannot be measured from the files.
deviations: Two sessions of 28, the only ones with pulse times.
The files hold only part of the pulses, so the offsets between pulses are measured on the deposited ones.

outcomes.statement: Of 822 pyramidal neurons, 611 responded to light from the uLEDs.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 2; Figure 1E
outcomes.quote: Of 822 neurons, 611 responded unequally to the three neighboring μLEDs
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b), all stimulation epochs, 66 of 91 putative pyramidal cells (72.5%, 95% interval 62.2 to 81.4%) respond to at least one uLED. Under reading (a), the PreStim epoch, 57 of 91 (62.6%, 51.9 to 72.6%), outside tolerance. Of 364 unit and uLED tests in PreStim, 68 pass all three parts of the test; on sham onsets (jittered by up to 200 ms, or moved into BaselinePre) none of 364 passes. For reading (b), with the onsets of all stimulation epochs jittered by up to 200 ms, none of 364 tests passes either. No putative pyramidal cell on shank Group3 responds (0 of 17), and that shank's uLEDs are likely among those whose pulses are not in the files. Without Group3, 57 of 74 (77.0%) under (a), within tolerance, and 66 of 74 (89.2%) under (b), above it. The criterion lists (a) first but only (b) matches, so the measured value is that of (b).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse (91 putative pyramidal cells), not 822 cells.

The response test is the one in the first author's later code (HippoCookBook getuLEDResponse.m), with 500 bootstrap sets drawn on a 1 ms grid and shared across units, and a minimum of 1000 pulses per uLED in place of 2000; the paper's own test is in its unavailable Methods.
Which pulses the paper tested is not stated; two readings are shown and the claim matches under reading (b) only.
Cells near uLEDs whose pulses are not in the files cannot be tested for a response to them.

outcomes.statement: Light-induced spike responses of individual pyramidal cells decreased during sharp-wave ripples (n = 485 neurons, P < 1e-55, Wilcoxon paired signed-rank test).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 3; Figure 1, F to I
outcomes.quote: light-induced spike responses in individual pyramidal cells decreased during SPW-Rs (ΔRate; Fig. 1, F to I).
outcomes.notes: In 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells, light minus control rate is 0.30 Hz (median) in windows overlapping ripples and 2.68 Hz outside, lower inside in 49 of 57 (Wilcoxon p = 6.8e-09), and in each session (p = 7.8e-06 and 9.5e-07). As a ratio, 1.25 inside and 2.89 outside (53 of 56, p = 8.6e-10). The paper's n of 485 and P < 1e-55 cannot be reached with two sessions. The control windows, the 20 ms before each onset, are dark under the stated protocol, so the missing pulses do not enter them.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.
Ripples are the deposited ripple intervals; a window counts as inside a ripple when it overlaps one.
Control windows are the 20 ms before each pulse with no uLED on.

outcomes.statement: The firing-rate change of pyramidal neurons during SPW-Rs is negatively correlated with their baseline firing rate (rho = -0.19, P < 1e-7).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 3 (figure S10)
outcomes.quote: the negative correlation between firing-rate change during SPW-R and baseline firing rates of neurons
outcomes.notes: Over 1166 putative pyramidal cells of 24 sessions, the log2 ratio of the rate inside ripples to outside is negatively correlated with the baseline rate (rho = -0.437, p = 1.8e-55). It is negative in every subject (-0.37 to -0.71) and every session, and significant in all sessions but three (fCamk1 sess13 p = 0.12, fCamk3 sess13 p = 0.29, fCamk5 sess14 p = 0.81). This is stronger than -0.19 and outside the tolerance of 0.068. The difference reading gives rho = -0.002 (p = 0.95). Without the two sessions in the analysis whose ripples fail the clock check (the third has under 50 first-epoch ripples), n = 1055 and rho = -0.468; in the 22 sessions whose first epoch is labelled BaselinePre, -0.450; against the rate outside ripples, -0.466.
deviations: The paper's measure of rate change is in the unavailable supplement; two readings were fixed before the analysis and they disagree.
The tolerance is the sampling half-width at n = 822, not 10% of the value.

outcomes.statement: During track running, the light-induced rate gain is largest at the trough of the theta cycle (P < 1e-6, Wilcoxon test).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4; Figure 2, A and B
outcomes.quote: We observed a gain at the trough of the theta cycle, the phase corresponding to the strongest synchrony of pyramidal neurons (Fig. 2A)
outcomes.notes: In 57 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells during laps, the gain is 2.04 Hz in the trough half of theta and 2.07 Hz in the peak half (medians), higher at the trough in 22 of 57 cells (Wilcoxon p = 0.14) and significant in neither session. In 60-degree bins the gain is largest 30 degrees after the peak (2.13 Hz). The stored LFP rate is 1250 Hz from 0 s and the LFP ends with the last epoch; ripple-band power at 44 and 27 deposited ripple peaks inside the Maze epoch is 113 and 78 times its mean; spikes of putative pyramidal cells in control windows have a circular mean phase of 128 and 130 degrees, in the trough half; the theta-band LFP averaged around onsets deviates by at most 27.1 and 8.5 against a theta-band SD of 406 and 770.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.
The LFP channel (largest ripple power), the theta band (6 to 10 Hz) and the half-cycle split are choices made here; the paper's are in its unavailable Methods.

outcomes.statement: More than half of the pyramidal neurons were place cells, 73% of light-responsive and 71% of non-responsive neurons, with no difference between them (P = 0.90, chi-squared test).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4 (figure S11)
outcomes.quote: more than half of the pyramidal neurons were classified as place cells [73% and 71% of light-responsive and nonresponsive neurons, respectively; P = 0.90, χ2 test
outcomes.notes: 48 of 57 light-responsive (84.2%, 95% interval 72.1 to 92.5%) and 24 of 34 non-responsive (70.6%, 52.5 to 84.9%) putative pyramidal cells are place cells; the paper's chi-squared test finds no difference (p = 0.20), as in the paper. The non-responsive fraction is within tolerance, the responsive one above it. Per session 83% against 56% (sess9) and 86% against 83% (sess12). Over all putative pyramidal cells 79.1% are place cells. With all time without a deposited pulse as control time and the earlier field rule (the round-1 analysis) the fractions are 78.9% and 52.9% with p = 0.018; the control time alone changes 5 cells, the field rule alone 1, both 11. Some non-responsive cells may respond to uLEDs whose pulses are not in the files.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.

Place fields follow a port of buzcode's bz_findPlaceFields1D with its defaults, on control maps from the windows dark under the stated protocol (the 20 ms before each deposited onset and after each offset), since most pulses are not in the files; the paper's standard definition is in its unavailable Methods. The files do not follow the protocol exactly (3.2% and 3.8% of deposited offsets in PreStim are under 20 ms), so missing pulses may fall in some of these windows.

outcomes.statement: The light-induced rate increase is higher within than outside the place field (n = 553 place fields, P < 1e-115, Wilcoxon test).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4; Figure 2, C to E
outcomes.quote: The induced rate increase was higher within than outside the place field (Fig. 2E and fig. S12).
outcomes.notes: Over 80 control place fields of 48 light-responsive putative pyramidal cells, gain is 3.95 Hz in the field and 1.37 Hz outside (medians), higher in the field for 61 of 80 (Wilcoxon p = 1e-08) and in each session (p = 9.5e-07 and 0.0018). As a ratio of light to control the in-field value is lower (2.19 against 2.77, p = 4.3e-05), so the increase is larger in hertz but not relative to the control rate.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 80 fields against 553.
Control rates come from the windows dark under the stated protocol.

outcomes.statement: The in-field gain is positively correlated with the out-of-field firing rate (rho = 0.17, P < 1e-5) and with the home-cage firing rate of the neuron (rho = 0.25, P < 1e-7).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 4 (figure S12)
outcomes.quote: This in-field gain was positively correlated with both the out-of-field firing rate and the home-cage firing rate of the neuron

statistics.about: in-field gain against out-of-field firing rate
in-field gain against home-cage firing rate

outcomes.notes: Over 80 fields, rho is -0.018 (p = 0.87) for the out-of-field rate and -0.063 (p = 0.58) for the home-cage rate, both outside tolerance. With one field per cell, rho is 0.131 for the out-of-field rate (within tolerance) and -0.003 for the home-cage rate.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 80 fields against 553.

outcomes.statement: Light responses in the home cage before the track were stronger in place cells than in non-place cells (P < 1e-4, Kruskal-Wallis test).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: Light responses in place cells, tested in the home cage before the track, were significantly stronger than in non-place cells
outcomes.notes: The PreStim light response (best uLED) has a median of 1.90 Hz in 72 place cells and 1.03 Hz in 19 non-place cells, higher in place cells but not significantly (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.19; z-scored p = 0.25). It is significant in sess9 (p = 0.027) and not in sess12 (0.94 against 1.19 Hz, p = 0.85). Within halves of the baseline rate neither difference is significant (p = 0.6 and 0.2).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 19 non-place cells.
Place cells as in figs11-place-cell-fraction.

outcomes.statement: Optogenetic depolarization revealed place fields in the majority of non-place cells, 289 of 417 (69.3%).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5; Figure 3, B and C
outcomes.quote: optogenetic depolarization revealed place fields in the majority of non-place cells (Fig. 3, B and C; 69.3%, 289 of 417
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), 7 of 9 light-responsive non-place cells (77.8%, 95% interval 40.0 to 97.2%) have a light field, 1.6 points above the tolerance of 69.3 plus or minus 6.9; under reading (b), 6 of 19 non-place cells (31.6%, 12.6 to 56.6%), below it and above the 15.8% found in control maps thinned at random to the time of the light maps. Reading (a) rests on 9 cells and its interval includes the paper's value. Its light maps use only each cell's own uLEDs (2.6% to 6.2% of lap time); control maps thinned to that time give a field in 31.7% of draws on average over the 9 cells.
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse; 19 non-place cells against 417.
The paper's denominator and its rule for an induced field are in its unavailable Methods; two readings are shown.

outcomes.statement: The spatial location of light-induced spikes matches that of spikes without stimulation, both for place fields of place cells (P < 1e-40) and for unmasked place fields of non-place cells, whose sparse control spikes form ghost fields (P < 1e-10).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 5; Figure 3, C and E
outcomes.quote: We found a robust correlation between the spatial location of induced place field spikes and the sparse spikes of non-place cells in the absence of stimulation (Fig. 3, C and E

statistics.about: place fields of place cells
unmasked place fields of non-place cells

outcomes.notes: For 70 field directions of light-responsive place cells the light peak follows the control peak (Pearson r = 0.806, p = 3.9e-17). For 14 light field directions of 7 non-place cells r = 0.321 (p = 0.26). In the shuffle variant, 35.7% of unmasked peaks lie within 4.4 cm of the control peak against 14.6% for shuffled pairings (p = 0.014), which is closer to the paper's test against shuffles. 8 of the 14 unmasked field directions come from sess9.
deviations: Pearson correlation of peak positions in place of the paper's chi-squared test against 500 shuffles, whose details are in the unavailable Methods; a shuffle test is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Place fields during light stimulation were more stable between the first and second halves of the session than during control epochs, for both true place fields and unmasked place fields (P < 1e-9 and P < 1e-19, two-way ANOVA).
outcomes.source: Figure 3F
outcomes.quote: Place fields during light stimulation were more stable for both true place fields and unmasked place fields

statistics.about: true place fields
unmasked place fields

outcomes.notes: Light maps are not more stable than control maps between laps 11-60 and 71-120 (place fields 0.664 against 0.714, light higher in 28 of 70, p = 0.058; unmasked fields 0.187 against 0.527, 6 of 14, p = 0.39). Against control maps from as many 20 ms control windows as light windows, place fields 0.664 against 0.602 (p = 0.68) and unmasked fields 0.187 against 0.293 (p = 0.67). Control maps from stimulated laps only give the same medians (p = 0.059 and 0.39), as they must, since dark windows lie only next to deposited pulses. The two-way ANOVA finds an effect of condition (p = 0.046), with light the less stable by the medians.
deviations: Control maps use the windows dark under the stated protocol (19% to 20% of lap time); the paper's control epochs were random 20 ms intervals between pulses, shown as a time-matched variant.
Wilcoxon tests in place of the paper's two-way ANOVA, which is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Spatial information of control and light-stimulated epochs is correlated, and the light-boosted increase is stronger for unmasked place fields of non-place cells than for place cells (P < 1e-15, Kruskal-Wallis test).
outcomes.source: Figure 3G
outcomes.quote: Correlation of spatial information (Bits/spike) between control and light-stimulated epochs ... Light-boosted effect was stronger for unmasked place fields of non-place cells than for place cell place fields

statistics.about: correlation of control and light spatial information, first of the two values printed
correlation of control and light spatial information, second of the two values printed
light-boosted effect, unmasked place fields against place cell place fields

outcomes.notes: Control and light spatial information are correlated for place fields (rho = 0.655, p = 7.6e-10) and for unmasked fields (rho = 0.574, p = 0.032). The increase is larger for unmasked fields (median 0.03 against -0.03 bits/spike, Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.039), far from the paper's P < 1e-15. Against time-matched control maps both correlations hold (place rho = 0.501, p = 1e-05; unmasked rho = 0.609, p = 0.021), but the increase is negative in both groups (place -0.10, unmasked -0.17) and does not differ (p = 0.3); as a ratio it does not differ either (p = 0.14). The paper's control epochs are random 20 ms intervals between the light pulses, which the time-matched variant follows most closely, and the dark-window control maps are themselves a revision of the criterion's control (all time with no uLED on). Part 1 holds and part 2 does not. Unmasked fields are chosen for a light field and no control field, which favours a larger increase by construction; the paper defines its groups the same way. Changed from reproduced after verification round 3 agreed.
deviations: Control maps use the windows dark under the stated protocol; time-matched control windows are a variant, under which the larger increase in unmasked fields does not hold.

outcomes.statement: Cofiring of place cell pairs during SPW-Rs in the home cage is positively correlated with their spatial overlap on the track (P < 1e-27), while pairs of a place cell and a non-place cell show no such relationship (P = 0.11).
outcomes.source: Figure 4C (legend); Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 4, B and C
outcomes.quote: SPW-R cofiring was positively correlated with spatial overlap in place cell pairs ... but not in pairs with place and non-place cell (non-PC) partners (P = 0.11).

statistics.about: place cell pairs
pairs of a place cell and a non-place cell

outcomes.notes: Over 1264 place cell pairs, ripple cofiring is correlated with spatial overlap (rho = 0.060, p = 0.032), so part 1 holds, weakly and in sess9 only (0.119, p = 0.0015; sess12 0.019, p = 0.66). Over 698 place and non-place pairs the paper's test finds no correlation (rho = 0.062, p = 0.1), so part 2 holds, but the coefficient is as large as for place cell pairs. Correlation of participation per ripple gives 0.054 (p = 0.056) and 0.072 (p = 0.058).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.
Cofiring as the Pearson correlation of spike counts per deposited ripple, a choice made here; the paper's measure is in its unavailable Methods.

outcomes.statement: With light-induced spikes, the relationship between SPW-R cofiring and spatial overlap appears for pairs that include non-place cells (P < 1e-5, Spearman correlation).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 4, C and D (legend panel D)
outcomes.quote: during optogenetic stimulation, the relationship between cofiring during SPW-Rs and spatial overlap was revealed for unmasked place fields of non-place field pairs (Fig. 4C).
outcomes.notes: Over 231 pairs of light-responsive place and non-place cells, cofiring is not significantly correlated with the overlap of light maps (rho = 0.075, p = 0.25; sess9 0.108, p = 0.16; sess12 -0.062, p = 0.65). With control maps the same pairs give rho = 0.110 (p = 0.094).
deviations: Two sessions of one mouse.

outcomes.statement: Stronger light (three intensities) decreased the light-induced response during SPW-Rs, increased the in-field gain of place cells several-fold, and increased the in-field gain of unmasked fields (Figure 1J, Figure 2F, Figure 3D; Friedman tests).
outcomes.source: Figure 1J, Figure 2F, Figure 3D; Main text, paragraphs 3 and 4
outcomes.quote: Increasing Vm depolarization decreased the light-induced response during SPW-Rs (Fig. 1J) ... Increasing depolarization of Vm by stronger light intensity increased the in-field gain several-fold (Fig. 2F).

statistics.about: response during SPW-Rs across light intensities, correlation (Figure 1J)
response during SPW-Rs across light intensities, all comparisons (Figure 1J)
in-field gain of place cells across light intensities, correlation (Figure 2F)
in-field gain of place cells across light intensities (Figure 2F)
in-field gain of unmasked fields across light intensities, all comparisons (Figure 3D)

outcomes.notes: The pulse series hold one value per uLED in each of the two sessions with pulses (19 in sess9, 62623 to 63599 in sess12, stated as watts), so no pulse has an intensity level, and the other 26 sessions have no pulse series. The paper's other named data location, the Buzsaki Lab Databank, serves data through Globus with an account and no pinned identifier.

outcomes.statement: Intracellular recordings in which the membrane potential was varied reproduce the decreased gain during SPW-Rs (five cells in anesthetized rats and five in head-fixed mice, P = 0.002).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 3; Figure 1, K to M
outcomes.quote: more directly by intracellular experiments, in which Vm was systematically varied (Fig. 1, K to M), reproducing the effect seen with optogenetic Vm depolarization (Fig. 1I)

statistics.n: five cells from five anesthetized rats and five cells from four head-fixed mice

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds extracellular recordings of four mice only; the intracellular recordings in rats and head-fixed mice are not in it. The lab's data page lists this dandiset for the paper and otherwise points to a Globus endpoint without a pinned identifier.

outcomes.statement: During SPW-Rs, excitatory neurons increased their firing rates more than inhibitory neurons.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 3 (figure S9)
outcomes.quote: During sharp-wave ripples (SPW-Rs), excitatory neurons increased their firing rates more than inhibitory neurons (fig. S9)
outcomes.notes: The units carry no cell type, and the no-raw-data files hold no waveforms. A rate threshold separates cells by the very quantity the claim compares, so it was not used for this claim. Waveforms could be taken from the raw signal, but the full files are 17 to 54 GB each and six of them have no raw signal. As a proxy shown in the notebook, units at or above 5 Hz raise their rate inside ripples less than putative pyramidal cells (median log2 ratio 0.75 against 1.19, p = 0.00065); since the ripple gain falls with baseline rate within putative pyramidal cells alone (figs10), this split would show the same without interneurons, so it does not test the claim.

outcomes.statement: Decoding of position is most accurate from light-boosted spikes of place cells, and light-induced spikes of non-place cells predict position better than control spikes of place cells (P = 0.001, Tukey test).
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 6; Figure 3H
outcomes.quote: The root mean squared error of the decoded position was highest for the sparse non-place cell spikes and lowest for light-boosted spikes of place cells. The induced spikes of non-place cells more accurately predicted the mouse's position on the track
outcomes.notes: The decoder, its spatial bins, time windows and cross-validation are described in the supplement, which could not be obtained; the main text and legend do not fix them. The data for it (two sessions with laps and pulses) are in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: ICA assemblies of place cells in the home cage show higher spatial correlation than chance, mixed assemblies of place and non-place cells do not, and with unmasked place fields they reach the level of place-cell assemblies.
outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 4, E and F
outcomes.quote: Assembly members of place cells, but not of mixtures of place and non-place cells, showed higher spatial correlation than chance (Fig. 4E). However, when spikes of unmasked place fields were considered, they expressed spatial correlation at the level of real place cells

statistics.about: assemblies of only place cells against mixed assemblies
interaction of assembly type and light stimulation

outcomes.notes: The ICA assembly detection (bin size, significance of components) and the chance level for spatial correlation are in the unavailable supplement. The legend gives only the member threshold of 2 SD. The data are in the dandiset for two sessions.

outcomes.source: Main text, paragraph 7; Figure 4, G and H
outcomes.quote: Sequential firing of place cells was correlated with spike sequences during SPW-Rs (Fig. 4G) ... The fraction of SPW-R events with significant virtual track trajectories increased when unmasked place fields were also included for the construction of the place field sequence template

outcomes.notes: The Bayesian decoding of ripples, the template construction and the shuffle are in the unavailable supplement; the legend gives only 500 shuffles. The data are in the dandiset for two sessions.

findings.statement: Light pulse times are deposited for 2 of 28 sessions (fCamk1 sess9 and sess12). Twenty other sessions name uLED stimulation in their epochs but hold no pulse series, so their light responses cannot be computed. Laps are also in these two sessions only.

The OptogeneticSeries are stated in watts but hold one value per uLED, 19 in sess9 and 62623 to 63599 in sess12, not a light power (the paper gives 0.02 to 0.1 uW). No light intensity per pulse is stored, so the paper's three intensities cannot be recovered.

The files hold pulse series for 6 of the probe's 12 uLEDs (Site3 to Site8), two of them with only 120 to 221 pulses, and most pulses of the protocol are missing. In PreStim the deposited pulses come at 5.76 and 7.50 per s, where the stated protocol implies about 17 to 25; in fCamk1 sess9 the offsets between deposited pulses fall only near multiples of 20 ms, the gaps left by missing pulses. No putative pyramidal cell on shank Group3 responds to any deposited uLED. Time without a deposited pulse therefore cannot be taken as dark.

Every session is deposited twice, as a full file and a no-raw-data file; in all 28 sessions the two hold the same units, spike times, ripples and position. The full file of fCamk3 sess20 is named sub-fCamk3_behavior+ecephys+image.nwb, without its session.
The full file of fCamk3 sess17 is 28 MB and holds 378 s of raw signal and 6850 s of LFP of a 34621 s session. The six full files of fCamk1 sess13 to sess19 hold the LFP but no raw signal.
Units carry no cell type and the no-raw-data files no waveforms, so pyramidal cells and interneurons cannot be told apart as in the paper.
session_start_time is 2016-03-15 in every file, while the session ids date the recordings to 2020 and 2021.
The linearized position holds values from 0 to 110 cm (the track length) but has a conversion factor of 100, which would put it at 0 to 110 m.

Six sessions (fCamk2 sess1 to sess4, fCamk3 sess13, fCamk5 sess10) name their epochs only by a time stamp, without behavioral paradigm or manipulation. fCamk2 sessions have no position and 0 to 1110 ripples.

The dandiset holds 28 sessions and 1351 units with a baseline rate below 5 Hz, where the paper reports 822 pyramidal neurons at 43.3 per session (about 19 sessions). It does not say which sessions the paper used. 14 sessions include CNO or DMSO epochs, which the paper does not describe.

In fCamk3 sess13, fCamk3 sess17 and fCamk5 sess10 the deposited ripple intervals mark population bursts weakly (population rate 1.2 to 1.98 times that 1 s later, against at least twice in the other 22 sessions with ripples). fCamk5 sess10 has 217 events with a median length of 109 ms.

The paper gives randomly variable 20 to 40 ms offsets between pulses, the files' description 40 to 60 ms. Measured onset to onset, 30% to 32% of the deposited intervals fall in 40 to 60 ms; measured end to start, 30% to 32% fall in 20 to 40 ms, and most others span missing pulses.

The paper's Materials and Methods are in its supplement. This attempt could not obtain the supplement from PMC or the publisher, and the analysis code the paper names (buzcode) is a general toolbox without scripts for its figures.

The paper reports 822 pyramidal neurons of which 73% of light-responsive and 71% of non-responsive neurons were place cells, which leaves about 230 non-place cells, but gives the unmasked fraction as 289 of 417 non-place cells.
The units table of some files lacks the shank column (group_id); columns are spike_times, unit_name, clu_id and, in the others, group_id.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper (PMC author manuscript). The verifier did not open NWB files; it tested find_fields and a simulated pulse protocol on synthetic inputs and read the archive's asset list. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; all 22 agree with the record as it then stood. The revision changed five outcomes, which round 2 reviews.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper (PMC author manuscript, saved as paper/PMC9632609_bioc.json and paper/PMC9632609.txt). It read the new find_fields but could not run it, as numpy was not installed. Report in transcripts/000568/verifier-2-report.md. Points not tied to one claim were also answered. The dark-window premise (round-2 remaining point 4) is now printed in the data check (3.8% and 3.2% of deposited offsets in PreStim under 20 ms) and stated in cell 12, the figs11 deviations and the summary. Point 3 (two sessions of one mouse) needs no change beyond what the notes state. Point 5 (Methods) cannot be answered, as the supplement is still unavailable.

disagreements.reason: Part 2 rests on p = 0.039 with dark-window control maps. Against time-matched control the increase is negative in both groups and does not differ (p = 0.3). The paper says random intervals (20 ms) between the light pulses served as control epochs, which the time-matched variant follows most closely. The criterion fixed time when no uLED is on, which the revision already replaced, so the main control maps are not the pre-registered ones either, and the selection bias still favours part 2.

entries.name: 000568-valero-2022
entries.title: Pulsed optogenetics in hippocampal CA1 (Valero et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Valero, Zutshi, Yoon and Buzsaki (2022) on dandiset 000568, which holds 28 sessions of CA1 units recorded with uLED probes in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice. Pulse times and laps are in two sessions only, so the light responses during ripples, theta and place fields are tested on those two; the ripple modulation of firing is tested on all sessions. The intracellular recordings and the light intensity levels are not in the dandiset.
